The **snub tetracontoctachoron** ([OBSA](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/OBSA): **snoc**) also commonly called the **snub icositetrachoron** or **omnisnub 24-cell**, is a convex [isogonal](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Isogonal) [polychoron](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Polychoron) that consists of 48 [snub cubes](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Snub_cube), 192 [triangular gyroprisms](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Triangular_gyroprism), and 576 [phyllic disphenoids](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Phyllic_disphenoid). 2 snub cubes, 2 triangular gyroprisms, and 4 disphenoids join at each vertex. It can be obtained through the process of [alternating](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Alternation) the [great prismatotetracontoctachoron](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Great_prismatotetracontoctachoron). However, it cannot be made uniform, as it generally has 4 edge lengths, which can be minimized to no fewer than 3 different sizes.

Using the ratio method, the lowest possible ratio between the longest and shortest edges is 1:         4 + 2   2   2   − 2    2       {\displaystyle {\displaystyle {\frac {\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2{\sqrt {2}}-2}}}}{2}}}}   ≈ 1:1.20627.

This polychoron generally has a doubled symmetry. A variant without this extended symmetry also exists, known as the [snub icositetrachoron](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Snub_icositetrachoron).

## Vertex coordinates

[[edit](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Snub_tetracontoctachoron?veaction=edit&section=1) | [edit source](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Snub_tetracontoctachoron?action=edit&section=1)]

Vertex coordinates for a snub tetracontoctachoron, created from the vertices of a great prismatotetracontoctachoron of edge length 1, are given by all even permutations with an even number of sign changes, plus all odd permutations with an odd amount of sign changes of:

- (     5 + 3   2    2   ,     1 + 2   2    2   ,     1 +   2    2   ,    1 2    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {5+3{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {1+2{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {1+{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {1}{2}}\right)}}  ,
- (  3    1 +   2    2   ,     3 + 2   2    2   ,     3 +   2    2   ,    1 2    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left(3{\frac {1+{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {3+2{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {3+{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {1}{2}}\right)}}  ,
- (     4 + 3   2    2   ,  ( 1 +   2   ) ,     2 +   2    2   ,  1  )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {4+3{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,(1+{\sqrt {2}}),\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,1\right)}}  .

An alternate set of coordinates, assuming that the edge length differences are minimized, centered at the origin, are given by all even permutations with an even number of sign changes, plus all odd permutations with an odd amount of sign changes of:

- (     4 − 2   2    4   ,     4 + 2   2    4   ,  ±    2 +   4 + 2   2      4   ,     2 + 2   2   +   20 + 14   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {\sqrt {4-2{\sqrt {2}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2}}}}{4}},\,\pm {\frac {2+{\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+2{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {20+14{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,
- (     2  4   ,       2   +   8 + 4   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   8 + 4   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   16 + 8   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {\sqrt {2}}{4}},\,{\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {8+4{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {8+4{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {16+8{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,
- (       2   +   4 − 2   2      4   ,  ±      2   +   4 + 2   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   20 + 14   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   4 + 2   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {4-2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,\pm {\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {20+14{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,

which has rhombic disphenoids (via the absolute value method), or

- (     2   2   − 2  4   ,     2 + 2   2    4   ,     2 +   2 + 2   2      4   ,     2 + 2   2   +   14 + 10   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {\sqrt {2{\sqrt {2}}-2}}{4}},\,{\frac {\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+2{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {14+10{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,
- (     2  4   ,       2   + 2   1 +   2      4   ,     2 +   2   + 2   1 +   2      4   ,     2 +   2   + 2   2 + 2   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {\sqrt {2}}{4}},\,{\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+2{\sqrt {1+{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+2{\sqrt {1+{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+2{\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,
- (       2   +   2   2   − 2    4   ,       2   +   2 + 2   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   14 + 10   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   2 + 2   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {2{\sqrt {2}}-2}}}{4}},\,{\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {14+10{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,

where the ratio of the largest edge length to the smallest edge length is lowest (via the ratio method).

The **snub tetracontoctachoron** ([OBSA](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/OBSA): **snoc**) also commonly called the **snub icositetrachoron** or **omnisnub 24-cell**, is a convex [isogonal](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Isogonal) [polychoron](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Polychoron) that consists of 48 [snub cubes](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Snub_cube), 192 [triangular gyroprisms](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Triangular_gyroprism), and 576 [phyllic disphenoids](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Phyllic_disphenoid). 2 snub cubes, 2 triangular gyroprisms, and 4 disphenoids join at each vertex. It can be obtained through the process of [alternating](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Alternation) the [great prismatotetracontoctachoron](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Great_prismatotetracontoctachoron). However, it cannot be made uniform, as it generally has 4 edge lengths, which can be minimized to no fewer than 3 different sizes.

Using the ratio method, the lowest possible ratio between the longest and shortest edges is 1:         4 + 2   2   2   − 2    2       {\displaystyle {\displaystyle {\frac {\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2{\sqrt {2}}-2}}}}{2}}}}   ≈ 1:1.20627.

This polychoron generally has a doubled symmetry. A variant without this extended symmetry also exists, known as the [snub icositetrachoron](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Snub_icositetrachoron).

Vertex coordinates

# Vertex coordinates

[[edit](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Snub_tetracontoctachoron?veaction=edit&section=1) | [edit source](https://polytope.miraheze.org/wiki/Snub_tetracontoctachoron?action=edit&section=1)]

Vertex coordinates for a snub tetracontoctachoron, created from the vertices of a great prismatotetracontoctachoron of edge length 1, are given by all even permutations with an even number of sign changes, plus all odd permutations with an odd amount of sign changes of:

- (     5 + 3   2    2   ,     1 + 2   2    2   ,     1 +   2    2   ,    1 2    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {5+3{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {1+2{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {1+{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {1}{2}}\right)}}  ,
- (  3    1 +   2    2   ,     3 + 2   2    2   ,     3 +   2    2   ,    1 2    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left(3{\frac {1+{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {3+2{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {3+{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,{\frac {1}{2}}\right)}}  ,
- (     4 + 3   2    2   ,  ( 1 +   2   ) ,     2 +   2    2   ,  1  )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {4+3{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,(1+{\sqrt {2}}),\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}}{2}},\,1\right)}}  .

An alternate set of coordinates, assuming that the edge length differences are minimized, centered at the origin, are given by all even permutations with an even number of sign changes, plus all odd permutations with an odd amount of sign changes of:

- (     4 − 2   2    4   ,     4 + 2   2    4   ,  ±    2 +   4 + 2   2      4   ,     2 + 2   2   +   20 + 14   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {\sqrt {4-2{\sqrt {2}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2}}}}{4}},\,\pm {\frac {2+{\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+2{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {20+14{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,
- (     2  4   ,       2   +   8 + 4   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   8 + 4   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   16 + 8   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {\sqrt {2}}{4}},\,{\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {8+4{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {8+4{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {16+8{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,
- (       2   +   4 − 2   2      4   ,  ±      2   +   4 + 2   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   20 + 14   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   4 + 2   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {4-2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,\pm {\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {20+14{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {4+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,

which has rhombic disphenoids (via the absolute value method), or

- (     2   2   − 2  4   ,     2 + 2   2    4   ,     2 +   2 + 2   2      4   ,     2 + 2   2   +   14 + 10   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {\sqrt {2{\sqrt {2}}-2}}{4}},\,{\frac {\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+2{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {14+10{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,
- (     2  4   ,       2   + 2   1 +   2      4   ,     2 +   2   + 2   1 +   2      4   ,     2 +   2   + 2   2 + 2   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {\sqrt {2}}{4}},\,{\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+2{\sqrt {1+{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+2{\sqrt {1+{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+2{\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,
- (       2   +   2   2   − 2    4   ,       2   +   2 + 2   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   14 + 10   2      4   ,     2 +   2   +   2 + 2   2      4    )      {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left({\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {2{\sqrt {2}}-2}}}{4}},\,{\frac {{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {14+10{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}},\,{\frac {2+{\sqrt {2}}+{\sqrt {2+2{\sqrt {2}}}}}{4}}\right)}}  ,

where the ratio of the largest edge length to the smallest edge length is lowest (via the ratio method).
